collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A child interviews elders about the past and finds they all remember it differently: record every version, or find the truth.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has been asking every elder about the day the great canoe sank, and every elder tells it differently. (friend) says (friend.his/her) version is the true one, because (friend.he/she) was there. So were all the others. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) carves every version on a long strip of bark, side by side. The elders read it and start arguing all over again, louder than ever. (subject) is very pleased.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) goes looking for evidence: the wreck, the old marks, the canoe's paddle in someone's hut. It turns out nobody remembered it exactly right. (friend) is annoyed, and also impressed.
